item.content:encoded:
Ethan Salas became the youngest MLB player with a walk-off hit since current Padres teammate Manny Machado in 2012.
Ethan Salas has only been in the majors for a few weeks, but he's already joining some impressive company.
In the process, the 20-year-old became the youngest MLB player with a walk-off hit since one of his current teammates, Manny Machado, accomplished the feat on Sept. 13, 2012.
"It's different, man," Salas told MLB.com. "You got 50,000 going ballistic for you and the boys ready for you if everything works out."
The moment continued a remarkable stretch for Salas, who was called up for the first time in early September.
His major-league career began quietly. Salas went hitless in his first 15 at-bats before tripling for his first MLB hit against San Francisco on Sept. 13.
Three days later, Salas' bat erupted.
He hit the first two home runs of his major-league career in a 9-3 victory over the Colorado Rockies. At 20 years and 107 days old, Salas became the youngest catcher in MLB history to hit two home runs in one game.
Saturday brought another milestone.
Manager Craig Stammen sent Salas to the plate as a pinch hitter with Cronenworth at third base and one out in the bottom of the 10th. Salas fell behind in the count before delivering the game-winning single.
"Good at-bat for him, fouled off a pitch, line drive right up the middle," Stammen told MLB.com. "That's what that kid can do."
The hit mattered well beyond Salas' place in the record book.
San Diego earned its 12th victory in 13 games and moved into sole possession of the second National League Wild Card spot. The Padres improved to 86-69 and moved another step closer to securing a postseason berth.
It has been a rapid progression for a player who didn't collect his first major-league hit until a week ago.
First came the triple. Then came the historic two-homer performance. Now Salas has his first walk-off hit and another connection to Machado in the MLB record book.
"Living the dream, man," Salas told MLB.com.

Francisco Lindor and Manny Machado continue to be two of the highest-paid infielders in Major League Baseball, both signed to nine-figure, long-term contracts. Lindor’s deal with the New York Mets extends through 2031, while Machado’s extension with the San Diego Padres extends through 2033.
The financial comparison is more than headline contract values. Their net worth includes their 2026 salary and all career earnings in MLB, as well as endorsements, investments and real estate holdings. However, specific personal net worth figures are not publicly available and are subject to estimation, not official disclosure.
Francisco Lindor and Manny Machado net worth comparison in 2026
Francisco Lindor and Manny Machado are also in the same ballpark of wealth, according to public estimates, in 2026. Lindor’s deal with the Mets has greatly boosted his wealth, while Machado has built up big earnings thanks to his contracts with the Padres and his previous MLB deals.
Celebrity Net Worth reports that Lindor’s current deal is for $341 million over 10 years, and it keeps him signed through the 2031 season. The deal Machado signed is bigger in total value at $350 million over 11 years and runs through 2033, according to Celebrity Net Worth.
| Financial category | Francisco Lindor | Manny Machado |
| Estimated net worth | $75M–$100M | $75M–$100M |
| Current MLB team | New York Mets | San Diego Padres |
| Current contract | 10 years, $341M | 11 years, $350M |
| Contract through | 2031 | 2033 |
| 2026 total salary/payroll figure | $32.48M | $25.09M |
| Average annual value | $34.1M | $31.82M |
Lindor’s financial foundation is a 10-year, $341 million deal with the Mets. Celebrity Net Worth said the deal averages $34.1 million a year and was designed to keep the All-Star shortstop in New York through the 2031 season.
According to Celebrity Net Worth, Lindor is ranked as one of the highest-paid players in Major League Baseball in 2026 with a total compensation of approximately $32.48 million. Career earnings projections have also climbed above $200 million, a nod to his time with Cleveland and New York.
Manny Machado wealth profile with San Diego Padres
Machado’s wealth comes from an elite MLB career and successive blockbuster contracts. Per Celebrity Net Worth, the Padres finalised his 11-year, $350 million extension in February 2023, keeping him in San Diego through the 2033 season.
The average annual value of the contract is approximately $31.82 million. His reported 2026 salary is about $25.09 million, according to Celebrity Net Worth. But the contract structure boosts his salary in later seasons, with Baseball-Reference listing an average of $39.1 million per year from 2027 to 2033.
Machado’s financial portfolio is not just his playing salary. His long career in the MLB, along with endorsements and property holdings, has helped establish other sources of wealth, although specific private investments and asset values are not fully disclosed.
Lindor and Machado contract earnings compared in 2026
The headline numbers give you a sense of how close the two financial profiles are, but they also reveal an important difference in the structure of the contract. Machado has the larger overall commitment at $350 million, according to Celebrity Net Worth, but Lindor has the larger average annual value at $34.1 million.
Lindor is also making more in 2026 than Machado is reportedly making. Celebrity Net Worth has Lindor’s AP-derived salary data at about $32.48 million for the season and Machado’s at $25.09 million.
| Contract and earnings category | Francisco Lindor | Manny Machado |
| Total current contract | $341M | $350M |
| Contract length | 10 years | 11 years |
| Average annual value | $34.1M | $31.82M |
| 2026 compensation | $32.48M | $25.09M |
| Contract expiration | 2031 | 2033 |
| Major MLB position | Shortstop | Third baseman |
That means the two are still among the highest-paid players in baseball. Lindor’s deal has the higher average salary, while Machado’s contract has the higher guaranteed amount and that extra year of contractual security. Their future net worths will also depend on taxes, spending, investment performance, endorsements and the value of assets accumulated from their careers.

item.content:encoded:
As Guardians chase playoff spot, Jose Ramirez records career RBI 1,000
CLEVELAND — Cleveland’s baseball franchise has never had a player quite like Jose Ramirez.
Along with signing under-market contracts to remain with the Guardians twice and the many memorable moments in a Cleveland uniform over the past decade-plus, his assault on the record books added another chapter Sept. 18 in a 5-3 win over the Athletics, which allowed them to retake the lead in the American League Central race with eight game remaining.
In that win, Ramirez went 2-for-5 with a home run and two RBIs, which gave him 1,000 RBIs in his career. In doing so, he became the 12th active player to reach 1,000 RBIs, joining Freddie Freeman, Paul Goldschmidt, Manny Machado, Giancarlo Stanton, Mike Trout, Bryce Harper, Nolan Arenado, Andrew McCutchen, Salvador Perez, Eugenio Suarez and Carlos Santana.
“Very important to thank God for that opportunity to play here in this organization and to be bale to achieve that,” Ramirez said through a team translator. “But the most important part is that we’re able to win today because you guys know what I really want to do here, which is win.”
Jose Ramirez stats
He’s also just the second Cleveland player to hit that milestone with the franchise, joining Earl Averill (1,084), whose playing career ended in the early 1940s.
It’s a significant line on Ramirez's Hall of Fame resume. The home run also brought him within three of becoming only the ninth player in MLB history to reach the 300/300 club for home runs and stolen bases.
“I like to use round numbers,” Guardians manager Stephen Vogt said. “It’s 10 years of 100 RBIs. When you break it down that way, it’s incredible what he has accomplished, and he’s not even close to being done. And very few people get do it, and it’s really cool to be here to watch it.”
It was a milestone night for Ramirez, though it came at the end of what has been one of his more frustrating seasons, particularly over the last few weeks while he’s played through hamate been surgery rehab.
Jose Ramirez injury update
He’s posted a 90 wRC+, which would be the first time since he became a full-time player in 2016 he’s been below 100 (league average). Since he returned to the lineup on July 22, after the procedure, he’s hit .216 with a .567 OPS.
“I keep working on it every day,” Ramirez said. “I have to keep working in the training room every day because this type of injury is the type where one day you feel good, the next you don’t feel so well, but you have to keep grinding.”
Despite the lack of his usual MVP-caliber production on a nightly basis, Vogt and the Guardians have still applauded the way Ramirez has fought through the situation. It’s one of the attributes that often gets mentioned first when listing why they feel he’s so valuable to the organization.
“Even as he was coming back and we have to give him off days, he was not happy about it,” Vogt said. “He wants to play every day. He wants to give us everything that he has on any given day. We know that there’s days where he’s not feeling good and he still goes out and gives 100 percent of what he has that day.
“It’s such a great example for our young guys to see that just because you’re not feeling 100 percent, it doesn’t mean you can’t go out and compete and contribute to help the team win.”
Ryan Lewis covers the Guardians for the Beacon Journal. He can be reached at rlewis1@gannett.com.

item.content:encoded:
CLEVELAND -- As the Progressive Field crowd roared around him, José Ramírez paused and leaned back in the left-handed batter’s box to admire his work. There was no doubt where the baseball he launched to right field was headed.
That image has played on repeat over the past 14 seasons. This time, it came with a heavy dose of history, and it was well-timed as the Guardians continue to push for the postseason.
Ramírez tallied his 1,000th career RBI on Friday by launching his 297th career home run, in the sixth inning of the Guardians’ matchup with the A’s in the opener of a three-game series. The superstar third baseman joined Earl Averill (1,084) as the only players in Cleveland franchise history to hit the RBI milestone.
The Guardians improved to 79-75 with their third straight win. They entered Friday with the same record as the White Sox, but Chicago technically led the division because it holds the tiebreaker over Cleveland after winning the season series.
It means the Guardians must finish with more wins than the Sox to win the Central for a third straight year. Ramírez helped; his towering blast went a Statcast-projected 401 feet and had a 102.4 mph exit velocity.
Ramírez, who turned 34 years old on Thursday, is now just the 12th active player with 1,000 career RBIs, joining Freddie Freeman, Paul Goldschmidt, Nolan Arenado, Manny Machado, Giancarlo Stanton, Andrew McCutchen, Carlos Santana, Bryce Harper, Salvador Perez, Mike Trout and Eugenio Suárez.
The home run was Ramírez’s first since Aug. 30 and just his 12th this season. He entered Friday with an uncharacteristic .683 OPS in 117 games, in an injury-impacted campaign after he missed five weeks following left hamate surgery.
Ramírez has been dealt with the effects of that procedure since he came off the injured list on July 22. On Friday, he reminded us he’s always just one swing away from impacting a game in a big way.
